name: Jezebel
source_summary: The Phoenician princess who married King Ahab, promoted Baal worship throughout Israel, orchestrated the murder of the prophets and of Naboth for his vineyard, and died a violently prophesied death.
family_friendly_summary: Jezebel was a princess from Phoenicia who married King Ahab of Israel. She was determined to spread the worship of the false god Baal throughout Israel and worked hard to have God's true prophets killed, forcing many of them into hiding. When a man named Naboth refused to sell King Ahab his family's vineyard, Jezebel arranged false accusations against him so he would be killed and Ahab could simply take the land. The prophet Elijah confronted Ahab and Jezebel directly about their wickedness and warned that serious judgment was coming. Years later, exactly as Elijah had prophesied, Jezebel met a sudden and violent end. Her name has become a byword throughout history for wickedness and the corrupting use of power and influence.
adult_story: Jezebel, a Phoenician princess, married Ahab, king of Israel, and used her influence to institutionalize Baal worship across the kingdom, supporting 450 prophets of Baal and 400 of Asherah at her own table (1 Kings 16:31; 18:19). She actively hunted down the LORD's prophets, forcing Obadiah to hide a hundred of them in caves to save their lives (18:4, 13). After Elijah's decisive victory over her prophets at Mount Carmel, Jezebel sent a death threat that drove Elijah into the wilderness in despair (19:1-4). Her most notorious act came when Ahab sulked over Naboth's refusal to sell his vineyard: Jezebel arranged false witnesses to accuse Naboth of blasphemy, had him stoned to death, and handed the vineyard to Ahab, prompting Elijah's direct pronouncement that dogs would eat Jezebel's flesh by the wall of Jezreel (21:1-16, 23). Years later, when Jehu came to purge Ahab's dynasty, Jezebel painted her eyes and dressed her hair to face him down defiantly from a window, but Jehu had her thrown down; her body was trampled by horses and eaten by dogs before it could be buried, leaving nothing but her skull, feet, and hands, exactly as Elijah had prophesied (2 Kings 9:30-37). Jezebel's name became lasting biblical shorthand for idolatry, persecution of the faithful, and ruthless abuse of royal power (Revelation 2:20).
christ_connections: Jezebel's persecution of God's true prophets, forcing many into hiding, previews the pattern of hostility the world would later show to Christ Himself and to His followers (John 15:20).

Jezebel's violently prophesied and precisely fulfilled downfall demonstrates that God's justice, though it may delay, is certain -- the same certainty that guarantees final judgment will one day be set right through Christ (Acts 17:31).
devotionals: Jezebel’s story warns us about idolatry; may we look to Jesus, whose grace and truth never fail.
Through Jezebel’s experience of persecution, God teaches us to trust His wisdom and follow Jesus faithfully.
